description: Born from the fusion of BioMicelio and Prodigios, we are one team of young Amazonian innovators. BioMicelio, national champion of INNOVaiLAB, contributes biocommerce and AI-driven mushroom tourism through MicoRuta Pastaza. Prodigios, second place in Expo Clean's Challenge 5, contributes computer vision and prototyping through JaguAR. Together, we turn biodiversity, business thinking and artificial intelligence into sustainable solutions for the Amazon.
summary: Willak.space combines NASA open data, field measurements and the knowledge of Kichwa families to decide what to plant and how to rotate the Amazonian chakra (a diversified family plot) in Napo, Ecuador. It is built for the agroecologists and field technicians who work with those families. For each plot, the app downloads NASA data for that coordinate, computes five traffic-light risks (heat, soil moisture, heavy rain, dry spells, erosion), reads the greenness (EVI) series since 2001 to detect the stage of the chakra, recommends what to plant with a 0–100 score across five planting systems, and builds a rotation plan that keeps the soil covered during the heavy-rain months. What the family says overrides what the satellite detects. It addresses the challenge “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data” by turning satellite data into decisions a small Amazonian farm can act on, in Spanish and English, and it works offline as a progressive web app. It is important because most farm tools are built for monocultures, not for diverse chakras where the family’s knowledge is the main source of truth.
details:
What it does. Willak.space is a decision tool for the Amazonian chakra. For each plot (a coordinate chosen on the map) it:

  1. Downloads NASA data for that point.
  2. Computes five risks with a traffic light: extreme heat, root-zone moisture, heavy rain, dry spells and erosion.
  3. Reads the MODIS greenness (EVI) series since 2001, detects the stage of the chakra and shows the recovery percentage against a stable-forest reference within 5 km.
  4. Recommends what to plant with a 0–100 score over five planting systems. Weights: rotation 40, soil 25, climate 20, family priorities 15.
  5. Builds a rotation plan that keeps the soil covered in the heavy-rain months.
  6. Raises an alert when greenness deviates −15 % or more from what is expected for the crop.

What the family says always overrides what the satellite detects.

How it works.

  • Quality control: cloudy or shadowed pixels are discarded using pixel_reliability and VI_Quality. If less than 50 % of the plot is valid, the date is marked as missing.
  • Spatial weighting: each 250 m MODIS pixel is weighted by the fraction that falls inside the plot.
  • Terra + Aqua merge: one value every 8 days.
  • Smoothing: Whittaker (λ = 50) fitted to the upper envelope (Eilers, 2003). Only gaps of up to 48 days are filled, and every filled point is flagged.
  • Slope: Horn’s method on SRTM (Horn, 1981).
  • The recommendation engine is deterministic and rule-based, with no trained model. The same data always gives the same answer, and every threshold is in an open file (sitio/app/config.js).

NASA data. NASA POWER (live), NASA GIBS (live), MODIS MOD13Q1/MYD13Q1 v061, GPM IMERG v07, SRTM v3, AppEEARS, NASA Worldview and Blue Marble. Honest status: POWER and GIBS run live in the demo. MODIS, IMERG, SRTM and AppEEARS are coded and tested against a simulator of the services (35 server tests). A test with a real Earthdata account is still pending. The test plot uses illustrative data and is labelled as such throughout the app.

Benefits and intended impact. It helps agroecologists and technicians support Kichwa families in Napo to choose crops and rotations, keep the soil covered in the rainy season and detect problems early. It respects local knowledge instead of replacing it.

Tools. Framework-free JavaScript, Leaflet, progressive web app (works offline), serverless functions in Node (Netlify Functions). 92 automated tests (57 logic, 35 server). Open source under the MIT license. Hosted on GitHub Pages. Bilingual Spanish/English.

Creativity and factors considered. It combines satellite data with Kichwa knowledge. It uses two original mascots (an astronaut woolly monkey and a farmer woolly monkey) to make it approachable, and it is designed for low connectivity. We considered cloud cover over the Amazon, the small size of chakras compared with a 250 m pixel, and the need to be transparent about what is live and what is simulated.

AI use. Google Flow for images and video of the plants and the mascots. Claude (Anthropic) for coding, testing and documentation help. Microsoft Edge neural voices for the demo video narration. The project does not use the NASA logo and is not affiliated with NASA.
